r.name: Coast to Coast Walk (St Bees to Shap)
Miles without Stiles: Wray Castle to Loanthwaite
Windermere West Shore Walk, Claife Viewing Station
r.description: A wonderful lakeshore walk through woodland & parkland. The low-level linear route features views of the islands of Windermere, archaeology & the Victorian Gothic Wray Castle. Some short steep sections on tarmac, grass & gravel tracks.

r.name: Sizergh Fell, Sizergh
r.description: The traditional agricultural estate surrounding Sizergh offers views of the Lakeland Fells, Pennines & Morecambe Bay, as well as an array of animals, birds, butterflies & wildflowers. Mostly grassy paths, steep, uneven surfaces & gates.

r.name: Low Sizergh Farm Trail, Sizergh
r.description: See where your food comes from en route —passing the cows in the fields, the vegetable plots at Growing Well, and the fruit trees in the orchard.

r.name: Holeslack Access Trail, Sizergh
r.description: This circular offers a flavour of the Sizergh estate, from ancient woodland, traditional orchard, historic farm buildings & parkland. This is a Miles Without Stiles route, designed to be accessible & well surfaced for trampers, limited mobility & buggies.

r.name: Kendal to Sizergh along the River Kent, Sizergh
r.description: Walk along River Kent and Sizergh estate, dog friendly, Abbot Hall, Lancaster Canal Trail, Roman Forts, Suspension Bridge. Low Sizergh's barn, café and shop, check the website for opening hours.

r.name: Park End Moss Wetland Walk at Sizergh
r.description: Park End Moss was once an area of degraded farmland, now transformed into a wildlife haven. This circular takes you through ancient woodland to wetland, popular with a variety of bird species. NB: trail map on the website differs form leaflet.

r.name: Windermere to Townend walk, Windermere
r.description: Follow this walk to Townend, a 17th-century farmhouse in Troutbeck, which provides an insight into the local area. Views of the fells, a church with stained glass windows by Sir E. Burne-Jones & W. Morris. A challenging alternate return option available.

r.name: The Wray Castle to Latterbarrow Walk, Wray Castle
r.description: Starting and finishing at the Castle at Wray, this route through fields and woodland offers rewarding Lakes views without the big fell climb. Though there are climbs, including to the summit of Latterbarrow, road sections and descents.

r.name: Wray to Blelham Tarn Circular Walk, Wray Castle
r.description: Start from Wray Castle, taking in Blelham Tarn & return via Windermere shoreline. From the Ice Age to Iron Age, medieval monks to Victorians, this walk combines tranquil beauty, views & stories from the past. Low-lying areas are boggy in wet weather.

r.name: Epley Head Waymarked Walk, Wray Castle
r.description: Mostly wide, good gravel surface, 3 steep sections and a short section on grass. Route is suitable for trampers.

r.name: Beatrix Potter's Moss Eccles Tarn Walk, Hill Top
r.description: Gentle walk to 1 of Beatrix Potter's favourite places, Moss Eccles Tarn. This is where the children's author spent time painting & is a great introduction to the place included in her books. Short steep sections. Muddy in wet weather. Potential livestock

r.name: Ash Landing and Claife Heights Windermere Walk, Claife Viewing Station
r.description: An elevated walk along Windermere's undeveloped western side. Dramatic viewing point at Low Blind How, where a gap in the wall leads to a crag with views of the lake, islands & Troutbeck fells. Some steep slopes, but once on the Heights its generally flat

r.name: Fell Foot circular heritage trail, Fell Foot
r.description: Enjoy this circular Lake District walk exploring some of Fell Foot's heritage, including a complex of historic boathouses, a modern Active Base, and an 18th-century pleasure ground including a Pinetum. An easy walk on hard and grass paths.

r.name: Post Knott, Windermere Views Walk, Windermere
r.description: A short but steep climb taking you up to a variety of impressive views over Windermere & the stunning central fells of the Lake District, with plenty of resting places & potential picnic sites along the way. Steep in places, mostly roads & surfaced paths

r.name: Townend and Troutbeck Valley Walk, Windermere
r.description: Explore classic Lakeland scenery on this walk from Brockhole, near Windermere, through Troutbeck Valley to the historic 17th-century farmhouse, Townend. Along the way, take in fell views, spot wildlife & admire traditional Lake District architecture.

r.name: Ambleside to Troutbeck Walk, Windermere
r.description: From Ambleside, walk through country lanes, woods & fields. Get views of Windermere, visit Troutbeck village & Townend farmhouse, before returning to Ambleside via a more challenging route over Wansfell Pike with great views over the surrounding fells.

r.name: Wansfell from Troutbeck Walk, Windermere
r.description: Follow this challenging circular trail along old tracks and footpaths from Troutbeck to the fells. You're rewarded with outstanding views over Windermere and Ambleside from the top of Wansfell. Some rocky, uneven ground.
